why: The student reads 'if (x > 0);' as if the println belonged to the if, but the ';' is an empty statement that is the whole then branch, so "positive" is always printed (the code prints positive, negative, checked). This is the SemicolonAfterIfHeader wrong rule.

concepts.quote: positive is not printed, because x > 0 is false.
concepts.why: The rule that a false condition skips the body is applied to this code, but to the wrong body (println instead of ';'), so the prediction is wrong.
The student ignores the ';' after the header and reads it as 'if x is positive, do the next line', but that ';' is the empty then branch.
